Definition: (only in plural) a dismissal, i.e. (of a wife) divorce (especially the document); also (of a daughter) dower
BiblicalUsage: The word covers both sides of a parting: Jethro takes back Zipporah after Moses had sent her away, Pharaoh gives Gezer as a wedding present with his daughter, and Micah tells Judah to give presents to Moreshethgath as a parting gift. A sending away and the gift that goes with it are the same word.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is honest about what parting costs, because in the Bible a dismissal is never just a door closing — something goes with the one who leaves. I hold that God notices what we send away and what we send with it.
